Webb County's early voting total reached 29,892 ballots through the eighth day of early voting, the Laredo Morning Times reported — 29,207 cast in person and 685 by mail.

On the eighth day, Monday, voters cast 3,554 ballots — 3,466 in person and 88 by mail, the Times reported. Monday, Oct. 19, remained the busiest day of the first eight days at 5,343 ballots, while Sunday was the slowest at 1,913.

The Laredo Fire Department Administrative Center led all polling sites with 9,497 votes through eight days. On Monday, its top sites were that center (964), McKendrick Ochoa Salinas Library (509), and the City Hall Annex Building (498).

Through the first five days, voters had cast 20,637 ballots — 20,043 in person and 594 by mail — the Times reported Oct. 23. By the end of the first week, the total had passed 26,000 ballots, KGNS reported Oct. 26. The eighth-day total puts the county on pace toward the 40,000-ballot early-voting projection County Elections Administrator Jose Luis Castillo gave earlier in the period.

Early voting runs 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. through Friday, Oct. 30. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Unlike early voting, Election Day voters must vote in the precinct where they are registered.

The ballot carries 38 candidates across 22 contested races at the county, state and federal levels, plus one proposition, the Times reported. Proposition 1 is a non-binding advisory question asking whether the City of Laredo should support efforts to expand pediatric hospital services in the Laredo-Webb County community; it would not authorize a project, funding, or require county action.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "Nearly 30K ballots cast through eighth day of Webb County early voting," Oct. 27, 2026
  • KGNS, "Over 26,000 vote in first week of early voting in Webb County," Oct. 26, 2026
